board.drafts_imap_ok: {count} draft(s) also placed in your mailbox Drafts folder.
board.drafts_imap_partial: Some drafts could not be placed in your mailbox — the .eml files are still in the folder above.

board.import_text_label: Or paste the job text directly:
board.import_text_hint: Copy the full job advert — title, company, description — and paste it here.
board.import_failed: Could not read a posting — missing {missing}. Try pasting the full job text instead.
board.detail.no_selection: Select a role to see details.
col.title: Title
detail.contained_body: a kill term matched inside a longer role name. Check this before trusting the kill.
detail.gaps_none: Your evidence covers every stated requirement.
detail.not_checked_body: the description was truncated or silent on this. Treated as unknown, never as a failure.

draft.never_sends: Dawnlist never sends. You send it yourself.
draft.send_ready: Ready to send from your mail app
entitlement.keyring_unavailable: Dawnlist could not open this computer's credential store (Credential Manager on Windows, Keychain on a Mac), where your licence key is kept, and this copy has not been verified recently. Unlock or restart the credential store and try again — nothing has been cancelled.
entitlement.licence_inactive: This licence key is real but no longer active — the subscription has lapsed, been cancelled or been refunded. Renew the subscription, then run again; if you believe it should still be active, write to Apps@spencerfields.com. Your board and your brief stay open either way.
entitlement.mac_lapsed: The App Store says your Dawnlist subscription is not active — it may have lapsed, been cancelled or been refunded. Renew it in the App Store, then press Restore purchase in Settings. Your board, your brief and everything already on this Mac stay open.
entitlement.mac_not_subscribed: No App Store subscription has been confirmed on this Mac yet, so there is no job feed to read. Subscribe in Settings, or press Restore purchase there if you have already subscribed. Your board, your brief and everything already on this Mac stay open.
entitlement.mac_unreachable: Could not reach the subscription service to confirm your App Store subscription, and it has not been confirmed recently. Check your connection and try again — nothing has been cancelled.
entitlement.ms_lapsed: Your Microsoft Store subscription has ended. Resubscribe in the app to carry on.
entitlement.ms_not_subscribed: Dawnlist needs a subscription. You can start one in the app.
entitlement.ms_unreachable: The Microsoft Store could not be reached, so your subscription could not be confirmed. Dawnlist will try again.
entitlement.no_variant: This copy of Dawnlist was packaged without a valid edition marker ({variant}), so it cannot tell which store it came from and will not run the daily search. Reinstall it from where you got it. Your board and your brief stay open either way.
families.armed_now: {name} is armed. Matching roles there will be screened out for nothing.
families.body: When you reject two roles of the same kind at one employer, Dawnlist offers a rule: kill that function at that employer, but keep reading the others. Nothing is armed until you say so, and every proposal shows the rejections it was built from.
families.heading: Employers you have turned down
families.none: Nothing proposed yet. These appear once you have rejected two similar roles at the same employer.
families.stood_down: {name} stood down. Nothing there is screened out by it now.
funnel.narrow_search: this search matches more postings than one run can fetch — open Settings to narrow it, or split it into two smaller searches
funnel.screen_drift: screening removed {now}% this run (was {before}% last run) — open Settings → Screening to review your rules if this was unexpected
key.billing: Anthropic accepted the key, but the account behind it has no credit left. Add credit on the Billing page at console.anthropic.com, then check again.
key.forbidden: Anthropic recognised the key but refused it permission to use the models — usually a restriction on its organisation or workspace. Check the key's workspace at console.anthropic.com, or create a key in a workspace that allows it.
key.rate_limited: Anthropic is limiting requests on this key just now, so it could not be checked. The key itself may be fine — wait a minute and check again.
key.rejected: Anthropic rejected that key. Check that it was copied in full, or create a new one at console.anthropic.com.
key.unexpected: Anthropic did not complete the check ({name}). Try again in a moment; if it keeps happening, create a new key at console.anthropic.com.
key.unreachable: Could not reach Anthropic to check the key. Check your connection and try again.
menu.language_changed: Dawnlist will be in {language} the next time you open it.
menu.restart_setup_confirm: Go back to the first screen of setup? Everything you set up is asked for again, starting from the terms. Your board, your shortlist, your Anthropic key and any subscription stay as they are.
onboarding.aim_placeholder: A sentence or two, in your own words. What kind of role, roughly what level, where, permanent or contract, and the lowest salary worth a conversation. Anything you leave out, Dawnlist has to guess at.
onboarding.answer_placeholder: Your answer — leave blank if you would rather not say
onboarding.answers_added: {count} response(s) added to your background record above.
onboarding.answers_none: Nothing new to add — type an answer first.
onboarding.app_no_verdict: the assessment returned no verdict for this posting, so there is nothing yet to agree or disagree with
onboarding.blocker_decide: decide at least {needed} of the {total} postings ({decided} so far)
onboarding.blocker_sentence: {title} at {company}: you disagreed, so say what sentence, added to the brief, would have got this right — a correction without one will not persist
onboarding.blocker_short_sample: Dawnlist could not fetch enough live postings to calibrate against — {count} of the {needed} it needs. That is a setup problem rather than anything you have done: check a search is switched on and the feed is reachable, then try again.
onboarding.calibration_body: Here are ten live postings, with what Dawnlist made of each one. Correct anything it got wrong. Where you disagree, tell it what sentence would have got it right — that sentence goes into your brief, so the same mistake is not made in the next run.
onboarding.calibration_failed: Dawnlist could not fetch postings to calibrate against: {reason} You can finish setting up; calibration will happen on a later run, once it can read the feed.
onboarding.calibration_fetching: Fetching live postings and reading them against your brief. This takes a minute or so.
onboarding.calibration_no_feed: Dawnlist has no job feed to read yet, because there is no subscription or access code on this computer. You can finish setting up; calibration will happen once you have one.
onboarding.calibration_pending: Dawnlist has not been calibrated yet, so these verdicts rest on your brief alone and have never been checked against your judgement. Calibrating takes a few minutes: Dawnlist shows you ten live postings, you correct what it got wrong, and your brief learns from the difference.
onboarding.calibration_skipped: There were not enough live postings to calibrate against, so this step has been skipped — nothing you did. Dawnlist will offer this step again the next time you open it, once a search is switched on and the feed is reachable. You can finish setting up.
onboarding.calibration_skipped_few: Only {count} live postings came back, but {needed} are needed to calibrate. This usually means your search terms are too specific — shorter topic words (e.g. 'Hotel Strategy' rather than 'Head of Hotel Strategy') cast a wider net. You can go back, edit your searches and try again, or finish now and calibrate later.
onboarding.calibration_skipped_zero: No live postings came back from any of your searches. This usually means the search terms did not match anything the feed carries — try shorter topic words (e.g. 'Revenue Strategy' rather than a full job title). You can go back, edit your searches and try again, or finish now and calibrate later.
onboarding.close_unsaved: Dawnlist is still working on something, and what it has not finished would be lost. Close setup anyway?
onboarding.corpus_earliest_year: The earliest role found starts in {year}. If you worked before then, add it — early operational roles are what tell the screen which jobs you have actually done.
onboarding.corpus_none: No readable CV text was found — check the files opened correctly before continuing.
onboarding.corpus_one_version: Only one CV version was read. Different versions describe the same role in different words, and those differences are the evidence — add the older ones if you still have them.
onboarding.corpus_unreadable: Could not read enough text from: {files}
onboarding.disagreement: You disagree — Dawnlist said {app}, you say {user}.
onboarding.discard_sample: You have switched different searches on since these postings were fetched. Fetching a new set costs money for every posting it returns, and the decisions you have made here would be lost.
onboarding.docx_unpacks_too_big: this .docx unpacks to far more data than any document needs, so it was not opened
onboarding.draft_failed: Could not draft from your CVs: {reason}. You can write both documents yourself and continue.
onboarding.draft_no_cvs: Add your CVs first — go back to the first step and drop them in, or choose them there.
onboarding.drafted: Drafted. Correct anything that is wrong before continuing.
onboarding.drop_hint: Drop your CV files here — PDF, Word or plain text
onboarding.factsheet_label: Background factsheet — what may be said
onboarding.file_too_large: the file is {size} MB and the limit is {limit} MB — no CV is that large, so it was not opened
onboarding.files_unreadable: Dawnlist could not read those files: {reason}
onboarding.history_empty: No versions have been saved yet.
onboarding.ingest_guidance:
Drag in every version of your CV you still have — including the old ones, the ones tailored for a specific job, and the ones you think are out of date.

Do not tidy them up first. Different versions describe the same role in different words, and those differences are the evidence. A single polished CV is the least useful thing you can give this step.

If your CV starts part-way through your career, say so. Early roles are often cut from a senior CV, and the screen needs them: they are what tell it which operational jobs you have actually done, rather than only the ones you have managed.
onboarding.interview_body: Dawnlist has read your CVs and drafted two documents. Correct them — they are a starting point, not a verdict. The factsheet on the left is the only thing your outreach is allowed to claim about you. The brief on the right decides what gets surfaced in each day's run.
onboarding.low_signal: You agreed with everything, which usually means this sample was easy rather than that the brief is finished.
onboarding.no_brief_yet: There is no fit brief yet, so there is nothing for calibration to correct. Go back and draft both documents, or write them yourself, then finish.
onboarding.open_questions: Dawnlist could not tell, and has left these open:
onboarding.pdf_too_many_pages: the PDF has {pages} pages and the limit is {limit} — that is not a CV, so it was not read
onboarding.profile_body: Five quick questions so Dawnlist knows where to look. You can refine everything later in Settings.
onboarding.profile_country_hint: Pick a country from the list, or type a two-letter code (e.g. GB, US).
onboarding.profile_location: Where must the role be based?
onboarding.ready: Ready — your brief will be updated with what you taught it.
onboarding.searches_add_placeholder: Type a search term and press Add
onboarding.searches_body:
These were suggested from what you said you are looking for. They start switched off, because each one costs money per posting it returns — so switch on the ones that are real searches, and leave the rest. You can also type your own below.

Tip: search terms match as substrings inside job titles, so short topic words work better than full titles. 'Hotel Strategy' will find 'Head of Hotel Strategy' and 'Director, Strategy — Hotels', but 'Head of Hotel Strategy' will miss the second one.
onboarding.searches_none: No searches were suggested — but you can type your own below. Short topic words (e.g. 'Hotel Strategy') work better than full job titles.
onboarding.searches_titles_failed: Dawnlist could not suggest search terms automatically. You can type your own below — short topic words (e.g. 'Revenue Strategy') work better than full job titles.
onboarding.searches_nowhere: Dawnlist could not tell where you want the job to be based, so these cannot be switched on yet. A search with no location looks across the whole world, and every posting it returns is paid for. Go back and say where in your answer, or set it in Settings once you are set up.
onboarding.searches_off: Nothing is switched on, so the daily run will be quiet. You can carry on and switch one on later in Settings.
onboarding.searches_where: Every search looks in {where}. You can change that in Settings.
onboarding.sentence_placeholder: What sentence, added to your brief, would have got this right?
onboarding.terms_agree: I have read the terms and I agree to them
onboarding.terms_body: Dawnlist shows you job postings that come from a data supplier, and the terms cover what you may do with them. They are short. Dawnlist cannot be used without agreeing to them, so please read them before you carry on.
onboarding.terms_changed: The terms have changed since you last agreed to them, so please read them again.
onboarding.title: Dawnlist — setting up
refusal.no_brief: There is no fit brief yet, so nothing can be assessed. Finish setup from the Dawnlist menu, using Start setup again if you need to.
refusal.no_cv: Dawnlist has no copy of your CV to tailor. A tailored CV reorders your own document and never writes a new one. Choose your CV files and Dawnlist will keep a copy on this computer for every application from now on.
refusal.no_factsheet: There is no background factsheet yet, and every claim Dawnlist writes has to come from it. Finish setup from the Dawnlist menu, using Start setup again if you need to.
refusal.no_licence: No licence key yet, so there is no job feed to read. Enter the key from your subscription email in Settings. Your board, your brief and everything already on this computer stay open.
refusal.no_linked_posting: That opportunity is not linked to a posting, so there is no advert to write against. Applications are written from the posting, never from the company name alone.
refusal.no_posting: That posting is no longer stored on this computer, so there is no advert to write against.
refusal.no_searches: No searches are switched on. Open Settings and switch on at least one, then run again.
refusal.terms: Dawnlist's terms have not been agreed on this computer, or they have changed since. Open Dawnlist and read them: the postings it fetches come from a supplier whose licence requires it, so nothing is fetched until that is done.
refusal.unscoped: These searches are switched on but say nowhere to look, so they would search the whole world: {searches}. Open Settings and set where you want to work; it applies to every search at once.
reject.hint: Optional — helps refine your future results
reject.title: Why are you rejecting this?
rules.body: Before anything is read by a model, Dawnlist screens it against these terms. A posting killed here costs nothing; a posting that gets through costs a fraction of a penny to read. Start with none — add a term when you notice yourself making the same decision twice.
rules.conflict: Not added — this would have hidden a role you pursued:
rules.contextual_help: Words that mean something in a job title and nothing in a benefits paragraph. Matched against the title and company only.
rules.employers_help: Earned, not typed. Pursuing a role adds its employer here, and every later posting from them is read. Change the decision and it leaves again.
rules.heading: Screening rules
rules.strong_help: Signal anywhere — title, company or description. A posting matching one of these is always sent to be assessed.
rules.unsupported_help: Title terms that rule a posting out however good the employer. Checked first, and against every role you have pursued before it is accepted.
run.calibration_needed: Dawnlist has not been calibrated yet, so the daily search will not run. Calibrating takes a few minutes: Dawnlist shows you ten live postings, you correct what it got wrong, and your brief learns from the difference.
run.done: Today's run has finished and the shortlist is up to date.
run.error: The run stopped with an error: {reason}
run.fetch_failed: The job feed could not be read, so this run found nothing new: {reason}
run.incomplete_status: The last run did not finish completely: {note}. Jobs that were not fetched will be picked up on the next run.
run.key_problem: The run could not start because of your Anthropic key: {reason}
run.last_not_today: Last run: {when} — no run yet today
run.limit_reached: The job feed allows {count} refreshes a day, counted by the UTC day, and today's are used up. They come back at {reset} your time.
run.not_entitled: The run could not start because this copy is not licensed: {reason}
run.now_tip: Search now. Offered when today's run time has passed and nothing has run yet today.
run.offer: Today's run was due at {time} and has not happened yet. Choose Run now to search.
run.partial: The run finished, but not everything was read: {reason}
run.running: Searching — this can take a few minutes.
cadence.body: The follow-up cadence controls when and how Dawnlist suggests you contact each person. Each rung fires after the gap below, and Tuesday/Thursday-only keeps your messages out of Monday inboxes and Friday close-of-business.
cadence.heading: Follow-up cadence
schedule.body: Dawnlist searches once a day, at the time below, while it is running on this computer. If that time passes with Dawnlist closed, it offers you Run now the next time you open it rather than spending anything without asking.
schedule.heading: When Dawnlist runs
schedule.keep_off: Closing the window will now quit Dawnlist, so no run happens while it is closed.
schedule.keep_on: Closing the window will now leave Dawnlist running. Quit it from its icon in the system tray or menu bar.
schedule.keep_running: Keep Dawnlist running in the background so runs happen on time
schedule.no_tray: This desktop has no system tray, so there would be no way back to a hidden window.
schedule.sign_in: Start Dawnlist in the background when you sign in
schedule.sign_in_login_items: macOS asks you to allow this yourself. System Settings has been opened: switch Dawnlist on under Login Items.
schedule.sign_in_off: Dawnlist will not start when you sign in.
schedule.sign_in_on: Dawnlist will start in the background when you sign in.
schedule.sign_in_policy: Whoever manages this computer has decided this, so it cannot be changed here.
schedule.sign_in_startup_apps: Windows asks you to switch this on yourself. Startup apps has been opened: switch Dawnlist on there.
searches.body: Each search below is swept in the daily run, at the run time set further down this page (while Dawnlist is open). Switched-on searches cost credits — 1 credit per job posting returned — so Dawnlist's suggestions start switched off until you review them.
searches.cost_summary: Your {queries} active search{qs} will make {calls} API call{s} per day ({both} search{qs} use 'both' mode = 2 calls each). Each call can return up to {page} postings (1 credit each).
searches.cost_summary_simple: Your {queries} active search{qs} will make {calls} API call{s} per day. Each call can return up to {page} postings (1 credit each).
searches.both_warning: 'Title and description' makes two API calls per search — one for titles, one for descriptions — doubling that search's daily cost.
searches.heading: What Dawnlist looks for
searches.needs_where: {label} cannot be switched on until you set where you want to work. With no location it would look across the whole world.
searches.needs_where_first: Set where you want to work before adding a search. With no location it would look across the whole world.
searches.placeholder: a job title to look for
searches.switched_off: {label} is off. Nothing will be fetched for it.
searches.switched_on: {label} is on. It will be swept in each daily run.
searches.where_empty: Enter where you want to work, for example: London, GB
searches.where_needs_country: Add the two-letter country code, for example: London, GB
searches.where_placeholder: City and country code, for example: London, GB
searches.imported: Imported {count} search(es). Imported searches start switched off.
searches.export_empty: Nothing to export — add at least one search first.
searches.cap_reached: You can have at most {cap} searches switched on at once. Switch one off before switching another on.
guide.imported: Applied {count} change(s) from the criteria guide.
guide.no_changes: No changes found — the guide matches your current settings.
settings.access_code_body: Given an access code, or already hold a Dawnlist licence? Paste it here and Dawnlist will use it. You do not need one if you subscribe through the Microsoft Store.
settings.admin_body: Issue override codes, and withdraw them. A code grants access; it never sells anything. Say who each one is for — an unlabelled code cannot be accounted for later. A code meant for an app reviewer must allow several uses: a reviewer may test on more than one machine, or re-test after a rejection, and a spent code turns that into a failed review.
settings.admin_confirm_revoke: Withdraw {code}? It stops working at once, and so does every licence already redeemed from it. This cannot be undone.
settings.admin_expires_tip: How many days the code keeps working. Only an administrator's own code, or one on the owner plan, may be set to never expire.
settings.admin_issued: Issued {code}. Copy it now; it is shown once here.
settings.admin_no_licence: No licence on this machine, so there is nothing to administer.
settings.admin_revoked: {code} withdrawn. It stops working on the next attempt.
settings.admin_uses_tip: How many times this code may be redeemed. Never 1 for a reviewer.
settings.code_redeemed: Code accepted — your licence is saved.
settings.code_store_failed: The code was accepted, but Dawnlist could not save the licence it gave you because this computer's credential store did not respond. Your licence key is {key} — copy it now and keep it, because the code may not work a second time.
settings.email_body: Connect your email account so Dawnlist can place drafts directly in your Drafts folder and learn your tone of voice from sent messages. Dawnlist never sends — you review and send each draft yourself.
settings.email_incomplete: Enter your email address and IMAP server.
settings.email_store_failed: The credential store would not save the password. Check your operating system's credential manager and try again.
settings.data_body: Job postings in Dawnlist are licensed from a third-party data provider. You can use them for your own job search, including keeping the ones you shortlist. You may not redistribute or resell them, or use them to build a competing job service. These limits continue to apply to postings you keep after your subscription ends.
settings.data_heading: Where the job postings come from
settings.key_body: Dawnlist reads job postings and drafts your messages using Anthropic's models, on your own account. Create a key at console.anthropic.com and paste it here. You can revoke it at any time, and Dawnlist stores it in your operating system's credential manager — never in a file.
settings.key_forgotten: Key removed. Dawnlist cannot run until you add another.
settings.key_none: No key stored yet — Dawnlist cannot run without one.
settings.key_store_failed: Anthropic accepted the key, but Dawnlist could not save it because this computer's credential store (Credential Manager on Windows, Keychain on a Mac) did not respond. Nothing was saved. Check the credential store, then press Save and check again.
settings.licence_body: Paste the licence key from your purchase email. If you were given an override code instead, paste that — Dawnlist will exchange it for a licence.
settings.licence_inactive: This licence is no longer active — the subscription has lapsed, been cancelled or been refunded. Renew it and Dawnlist will run again.
settings.licence_store_failed: Dawnlist could not save the licence key because this computer's credential store (Credential Manager on Windows, Keychain on a Mac) did not respond. Nothing was saved — check the credential store, then press Save again.
settings.licence_unknown: The licence service does not recognise this key. Check it against your purchase email.
settings.licence_unverified: Saved, not yet verified — the licence service could not be reached. Dawnlist checks again before the next run.
settings.offer_assigned: {code} — give this to {who}. Copy it now; it is easier to find here than anywhere else.
settings.offer_body: Give somebody free access to the Mac subscription. Codes are minted in App Store Connect and uploaded separately; this hands out what is already here. A code is redeemed on the recipient's Mac, so you do not need one yourself.
settings.offer_comp_done_off: Their licence will now end when Apple stops covering it. Anything Apple already granted still runs its course.
settings.offer_comp_done_on: Their licence will stay alive after Apple stops covering it. Nothing more for them to enter.
settings.offer_comp_not_eligible: This subscription was paid for, so it cannot be comped. Comping is only for people who came in on a comp offer.
settings.offer_comp_on: Keep access after the free period
settings.offer_confirm_void: Stop handing out {code}? It will not be given to anyone else from here. It REMAINS REDEEMABLE at Apple, which has no way to withdraw a code once minted, so anyone already holding it can still use it.
settings.offer_confirm_void_title: Take this code out of circulation?
settings.offer_empty: No codes here yet. Mint a batch in App Store Connect and upload it before giving any out.
settings.offer_nobody: Nobody has redeemed a code yet.
settings.offer_people_body: Who has redeemed a code and is using the Mac app. Comping someone keeps their licence alive after the free period Apple granted ends, so they never redeem anything again. Only a subscription that began with a comp offer can be comped; one somebody paid for never can.
settings.offer_pick_one: Choose a code in the list first.
settings.offer_pick_person: Choose someone in the list first.
settings.offer_voided: {code} will not be given out again. Anyone already holding it can still redeem it.
settings.offer_who_required: Say who this code is going to. A code nobody is recorded against cannot be accounted for later.
settings.report_body: Dawnlist uses generative AI to judge postings and to draft your messages. If it produces something inappropriate, offensive or plainly wrong, report it and it will be read.
settings.store_subscribe_detail: {title} — {price} a month. It renews automatically at the same price until you cancel, which you can do at any time in the Microsoft Store.
settings.store_subscribe_failed: The Microsoft Store could not complete that purchase. Nothing has been charged. Try again in a moment.
settings.store_subscribe_loading: Asking the Microsoft Store what this costs…
settings.store_subscribe_terms: Billed by Microsoft through the Microsoft Store. Cancel any time from Microsoft Store → Library → Subscriptions. You will still need your own Anthropic API key: reading postings and drafting messages bill to your account, not ours.
settings.store_subscribe_unavailable: The Microsoft Store cannot be reached right now, so the subscription cannot be started. This is not about your account — Dawnlist will try again.
settings.store_subscribe_unavailable_mar: This subscription is not sold in your country or region yet.
settings.subscribe_body: Dawnlist's job feed is a subscription, bought through the App Store. Everything already on this Mac stays open either way — your board, your brief and your tracker do not need a subscription to read.
settings.subscribe_deferred: Your purchase is waiting for approval — for example from the family organiser, under Ask to Buy. Dawnlist picks it up by itself once it is approved, so there is no need to buy again.
settings.subscribe_done: Subscribed. The feed reads for you from the next daily run.
settings.subscribe_still_waiting: The App Store has not answered yet. If no purchase window appeared, open the App Store app, check that you are signed in, then press Subscribe again. You can also restore an earlier purchase, or carry on and subscribe later.
settings.subscribe_terms: {title} — {length}. It renews automatically at the same price until you cancel it, which you can do at any time in System Settings.
settings.subscribe_unavailable: The App Store cannot take a purchase on this Mac right now.
settings.title: Dawnlist — settings
storekit.earlier_purchase_open: The App Store still has an earlier purchase of this subscription open, so it will not start another, and you will not be charged twice. If Apple's purchase window is not showing, restart the Mac and try again. If it is still open after that, sign out of the App Store app and back in.
storekit.not_ready: The App Store connection is still starting. Try again in a moment.
storekit.not_saved: Your subscription is confirmed, but this Mac's Keychain would not save it. Dawnlist will try again the next time it opens — you will not be charged twice.
storekit.nothing_to_restore: Nothing to restore on this account.
storekit.unconfirmed: The App Store has the purchase, but Dawnlist could not confirm it with the subscription service yet. It will try again by itself the next time Dawnlist opens — you will not be charged twice.
tray.still_running: Dawnlist is still running, so your daily run happens on time. Open it or quit from this icon.
update.body: This copy came from the website, so updates arrive from there too. The download page has the new version, signed, with its checksum published beside it. Nothing on this machine changes until you install it yourself.
update.title: Update available
voice.no_profile: No tone profile yet — add some of your own sent emails
voice.profile_from: Tone learned from {count} of your own sent messages
